summary: This manuscript presents a formalized, machine-checked set of negative results ('walls') regarding specific approaches to achieving volume-uniform Combes-Thomas coercivity in 4D SU(N_c) lattice Yang-Mills theory. Using Lean 4, the author demonstrates that a flat Hodge/block-Poincaré inequality fails to yield volume-uniform constants when using an unscaled line-integral block map and unweighted coarse norm. The paper proves two distinct obstructions: one in the constant sector (where the volume dependence forces a diverging bound) and one in the fluctuation sector (using a specially constructed half-period square-wave mode that yields a diverging Rayleigh lower bound). The work is highly rigorous, explicitly proving non-vacuity of its SU(n) adjoint models and providing an exhaustive theorem-to-code mapping. While strictly a negative navigational result concerning a highly specific mathematical normalization, it provides significant value for constructive Yang-Mills formalization efforts by definitively closing a plausible route. Static inspection confirms exemplary alignment between mathematical claims, quantifier discipline, and listed formal artifacts.
weaknesses: The negative results apply exclusively to one specific normalization (unscaled map with unweighted coarse norm), meaning the 'walls' can theoretically be bypassed by rescaling the block operator.
